post.description: Exchanges an email address and password for an access token and a new session. The Web client accepts only administrators and receives the refresh token in the fs_refresh cookie; the Mobile client accepts only technicians and receives it in the body.
Rotates the refresh token and issues a new access token. The Web client sends no body, the fs_refresh cookie and the X-FieldService-Csrf header; the Mobile client sends its refresh token in the body.

Revokes the session that the refresh credential belongs to. The Web client sends the fs_refresh cookie and the X-FieldService-Csrf header, and the response clears the cookie; the Mobile client sends its refresh token in the body. A missing, unknown, expired or revoked credential also returns 204.

Issues a ticket for one connection attempt to the notification service's Socket.IO endpoint. The ticket is valid for 60 seconds and is accepted once; every call issues a new ticket. Send no body. The access token's session must still be live and its user active; a revoked or expired session, or an inactive user, returns 401 auth.session-expired.

get.description: Returns the dashboard's figures in one read. The open job counts describe the current state, independent of the window. The range counts the jobs created, completed and cancelled inside the window, which starts at from (inclusive) and ends at to (exclusive). Both are required instants with Z or a numeric offset; to must be after from, and the window may span at most 31 days. The technician counts include active technicians only. Needs a technician lists at most the 10 earliest-scheduled Unassigned jobs, and recent activity lists at most the 6 newest history entries inside the window, newest first.
Returns every technician, ordered by name, with trade, shift, whether they can be assigned now, their count of open jobs, their current job in progress or on hold, and their next assigned job.

Returns the jobs assigned to the calling technician, and never another technician's. The active view, the default, holds Assigned, InProgress and OnHold jobs ordered by scheduled start, then job number. The completed view holds Completed and Cancelled jobs ordered by last update with the newest first, at most 50.

post.description: Creates a job with the next job number and a Created history entry. Without a technician the job starts Unassigned. With a technician, who must be active and on shift, it starts Assigned and also gets an Assigned history entry at the same instant. The response carries the job's details and version, and its Location header points to the job.

get.description: Returns one page of jobs that match every filter, ordered by last update with the newest first, with the total count and the count for each status under every filter except status. The search matches the job number, title, customer and site address.
Returns the job with its assignee, its complete history, oldest first, and the version to send with the next command. A technician can read only the jobs assigned to them; any other job returns 404.

put.summary: Assign a job to a technician
put.description: Assigns an unassigned job, or reassigns an assigned job, to an active technician who is on shift, and adds an Assigned history entry. Send the version you last read; assigning the same technician again returns the job unchanged. The response carries the job's details and its new version.

put.summary: Update the status of a job
put.description: Starts, puts on hold or resumes a job assigned to the calling technician, and adds a Started, PutOnHold or Resumed history entry. The status must be InProgress or OnHold. Putting a job on hold needs a note of at most 500 characters; a note sent with InProgress is not stored. Send the version you last read; sending the job's current status returns the job unchanged. A technician can change only the jobs assigned to them; any other job returns 404. The response carries the job's details and its new version.

post.description: Completes an InProgress job assigned to the calling technician and submits its inspection in one transaction, and adds a Completed history entry. Every checklist item must have a saved answer; otherwise the response is 409 inspection.incomplete. The site safety confirmation must be true, and the technician notes hold at most 2000 characters. A job that is not InProgress returns 409 job.invalid-transition; a job on hold must be resumed first. Send the version you last read; submitting a job that is already Completed returns the job unchanged. The job and its inspection are read-only afterwards. A technician can submit only the jobs assigned to them; any other job returns 404. The response carries the job's details and its new version.

Cancels a job that is Unassigned, Assigned, InProgress or OnHold, sets its cancellation time and adds a Cancelled history entry with the reason as its note. The reason is required and holds at most 500 characters. A Completed job returns 409 job.invalid-transition. Send the version you last read; cancelling a job that is already Cancelled returns the job unchanged and the reason is not stored. The job keeps its assigned technician and becomes read-only, and a draft inspection stays unsubmitted and can no longer be changed. The response carries the job's details and its new version.

get.summary: Get the inspection of a job
get.description: Returns the checklist of the job's template with every item and its reading fields in position order, the saved answers with their readings, the progress with the count of each result, the submission state, the technician notes and the job's version. It returns the checklist before the first save too, with every answer null and updatedAt null. A technician can read only the inspections of jobs assigned to them; any other job returns 404.

put.summary: Save the inspection of a job
put.description: Saves any subset of answers to the job's checklist as a draft; the first save creates the inspection. Each listed answer replaces that item's saved answer, readings included; unlisted items stay as they are, and an answer cannot be cleared. Send 1 to 100 answers, each for a different item of the job's checklist. A Fail needs a note and may carry any of the item's readings; a Pass supplies every reading field of its item once; a NotApplicable answer takes no readings. An answer holds a note of at most 1000 characters and at most 10 readings, each from -99999999.99 to 99999999.99 with at most two decimal places. A save changes the job's version. Send the version you last read; a save in which every answer equals the saved one returns the inspection unchanged. A job that is not InProgress, or an inspection that was submitted, returns 409 inspection.locked. A technician can save only the inspections of jobs assigned to them; any other job returns 404. The response carries the inspection and the job's new version.

get.description: Returns every checklist template, ordered by name, with its trade and item count. The create-job form offers them as the job's checklist.

post.description: Records an error from the web dashboard in the API log as one Warning entry with the source web and the caller's user id. The message, source and stack are scrubbed of tokens, secrets, email addresses and query strings before they are logged. The message holds at most 500 characters, the source and the route at most 200, and the stack at most 2000; the route is the path only, without a query string or fragment. The body holds at most 8 KB, and each user can report at most 10 errors a minute. The response has no body and echoes nothing.
